newsitem.title: UK: Steam power hits Rolls-Royce profits.
newsitem.headline: Steam power hits Rolls-Royce profits.

text.p: Engineer Rolls-Royce Plc reported a loss for 1996 on Thursday, hit by its decision announced last year to withdraw from the market for steam power generation equipment.

Rolls-Royce reported an overall pretax loss of 28 million British pounds ($45 million) after booking 263 million pounds ($424 million) of provisions, write-offs and losses that it detailed last year for its plan to sell or close its two steam power businesses. The loss compared with a profit of 175 million pounds ($282 million) in 1995.
Rolls put the two, Parsons and International Combustion, up for sale in July last year and said it would close the operations if it could not sell them.
But Chairman Sir Ralph Robins said on Thursday he was now close to selling both.
"There are several bidders for both...and we are confident that we are going to sell both of the businesses and that we will make some announcements in the next few weeks," he said in an interview.
Rolls said operating profits from its core aero-engines and industrial power businesses rose to 242 million pounds ($390 million) in 1996 from 178 million in 1995, boosted by strong order books.
Annual sales excluding businesses to be sold rose to 4.05 billion pounds from 3.34 billion pounds a year ago.

Robins said the company delivered around 1,100 aircraft engines last year and expected that this figure would rise in 1997 as output for commercial aircraft was set to be more than the 360 delivered in 1996.

"We will clearly deliver more this year," he said. "There is fairly significant growth in the civil business at the moment ... All the aircraft constructors are increasing their build rates and that's finally being reflected on us."
Robins also said the company was making progress in its attempt to sell Canadian subsidiary Bristol Aerospace and hoped for news "probably in the next few weeks."
The Winnipeg-based aircraft maintenance and rocket manufacturer has annual sales of around Canadian $60 million and employs about 1,000 people but was not considered a core business.
